title: The lock icon is not enough
brief: 18:25. Dan asks you to check tonight's run reached the bank. The top search result has a padlock and says Secure Login.
insight: The padlock means the connection is private. It says nothing about who is at the other end.
teaches: A padlock only means encryption: scam sites have one too
Read the real domain in the address bar before typing a password
Use the bookmark or the address you already trust, not a search result or an ad

value.title: Harbour Bank Business | Secure Login
value.text: Log in to Harbour Bank Business online banking. Protected by 256 bit encryption.

message.text: Sam, can you check tonight's run has reached Harbour Bank Business? Just search for it, my bookmarks are a mess.

setup.title: Chat
setup.body: Dan Whitlock: can you check tonight's run reached the bank?

outcome.label: Opened the padlock
outcome.what: The certificate is real, issued three days ago, to an address and not to Harbour Bank. The padlock only proves the connection is encrypted.
outcome.ideal: knows a padlock means private, not honest.

outcome.label: Read who owns the address
outcome.what: {{fake.label}}. The page is on {{fake.host}}, not business.harbourbank.co.uk.
outcome.ideal: reads the real domain in the address bar before typing anything.

outcome.label: Noticed Vault refused to fill in
outcome.what: Vault saved the bank login for business.harbourbank.co.uk, and will not type it anywhere else.
outcome.ideal: treats a password manager refusing to fill as a stop sign.

outcome.label: Went to the address you already trust
outcome.what: The bookmark goes straight to business.harbourbank.co.uk.
outcome.ideal: uses a bookmark or typed address for banking, not a search result.

decide.objective: Sign in to Harbour Bank Business to check the run, on the real site.
decide.insight: Anyone can get a padlock in minutes, for free. The part of the address just before the first slash is what you check.

hint.text: Search if you like, but before signing in click the padlock and “Who owns this?”. Try Fill from Vault: it only works on the real site. The Harbour Bank Business bookmark goes to the real address.

outcome.label: Signed in on the lookalike bank
outcome.what: The company's banking login went to the attacker, from a page with a perfectly real padlock.
outcome.ideal: reads the domain, not the padlock, before typing a password.

card.title: Private, not honest
body: The padlock was real. It meant nobody else could read what you typed, and what you typed went straight to the attacker, privately.
The address was {{fake.host}}, the certificate was three days old and issued to an address, and Vault refused to fill it in. The bookmark would have taken you to the real bank.
card.ideal: checks the domain before signing in, and uses the bookmark for banking.
card.rewindLabel: Rewind to before I signed in

outcome.label: Signed in on the real bank
outcome.what: business.harbourbank.co.uk, with Vault filling in the login. The run is there.
outcome.ideal: signs in only on the address they already trust.

card.title: The right address, the right bank
body: You signed in on business.harbourbank.co.uk. The sponsored result above it had a padlock too, on {{fake.host}}.
A padlock means private. The domain tells you who. Report the ad so it can be taken down.
card.ideal: reads the domain and uses the bookmark.

auto.text: Tell the bank and the service desk straight away.

hint.text: Raise a Helpdesk ticket under payment fraud so the bank login can be changed tonight.
